incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — high error rate in dedicated pool for customer KestrelBank (vpc-kestrel-01). Page sent to oncall (Priya Kapoor). Incident ID: INC-1836004321

Priya Kapoor: acked. I'm oncall — seeing elevated 5xx + timeouts on pool nodes serving KestrelBank. Primary mitigation in flight: scale up, route traffic to fallback models. 

Priya Kapoor: important: when we started digging, logs in the instance show unredacted account numbers and partial account holder names (PII). Need guidance before pulling logs out of tenant VPC for deeper triage.

Ethan Park: quick context — KestrelBank is on Dedicated pool 'aurora-dedicated-03', their config uses debug-level request logging. Default infra retention is 90d, but for VPC we follow customer retention which is 7d unless overridden.

Priya Kapoor: can we snapshot the logs into a secure bucket for analysis? I want to avoid emailing anything raw.

Maya Chen: do not copy unredacted PII out of the tenant VPC without Legal/Compliance sign-off. For immediate mitigation we can allow a restricted triage copy under strict controls: (1) list of authorized people, (2) KMS-encrypted bucket under Redwood account, (3) access logged, (4) retention limit (max 14 days) and proof of deletion. Who will need access?

Luis Ortega: I'll coordinate with KestrelBank contacts. We should also tell them we won't share raw logs externally. CS will provide the contact and get DPO looped in.

Priya Kapoor: authorized triage access requested for SRE (Priya Kapoor, Ethan Park) and Infra (Ethan Park). Maya — is that acceptable if we apply redaction rules during export? We can run redact-logs tool in the VPC before export. Example command:

```
# run in bastion inside the Kestrel VPC
/opt/redwood/bin/redact_logs --input /var/log/redwood/requests.log \ 
  --rules /etc/redwood/redact-rules/kestrelbank.json \ 
  --output /tmp/requests.redacted.log
aws s3 cp /tmp/requests.redacted.log s3://redwood-secure/kestrelbank/incidents/1836004321 --ssekms-key-id alias/redwood-incidents-kms
```

Priya Kapoor: redact-rules will mask account numbers (acct:\d{8,12}) and email addresses. We'll also drop full request bodies for any requests flagged with header X-sensitive: true.

Maya Chen: that process is acceptable as an emergency triage path. Conditions: a) run inside customer VPC (no external transfer of raw), b) redact rules reviewed by Legal (I've reviewed the kestrelbank.json preset), c) access granted only to named people, d) open a retention-override ticket in Compliance portal and attach approvals. We'll require that the S3 bucket be set to lifecycle delete after 14 days and that we capture the IAM audit log for who downloaded the file.

Ethan Park: starting redact pass now. I'll run in the bastion and post counts.

Ethan Park: ran `redact_logs` — summary: 1,248 account-number matches masked, 67 email addresses masked. Output uploaded to s3://redwood-secure/kestrelbank/incidents/1836004321/requests.redacted.log (kms: alias/redwood-incidents-kms). Lifecycle set: 14 days.

Ethan Park: audit note: `aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket redwood-secure --lifecycle-configuration file://lifecycle-kestrel-14d.json`

Maya Chen: good. Please also create an access control ticket that lists the IAM principals granted read access (use temporary STS sessions where possible). I need a compliance ticket link before we escalate.

Priya Kapoor: I'm documenting who accessed files. Command used to copy (inside VPC):

```
scp /tmp/requests.redacted.log ec2-user@infra-proxy:/tmp/ && 
aws s3 cp /tmp/requests.redacted.log s3://redwood-secure/kestrelbank/incidents/1836004321/ --ssekms-key-id alias/redwood-incidents-kms
```

Priya Kapoor: noting that we did not export raw logs. Only redacted copy left the instance.

Luis Ortega: I'll DM KestrelBank's security contact (A. D'Souza) and tell them we have a redacted snapshot for triage and that we will delete per 14-day retention. I'll request permission for Redwood to hold the snapshot temporarily for root-cause investigation.

Maya Chen: also required — send a short email to Compliance with: incident id, customer name, list of Redwood personnel with access, the S3 path, and the retention policy. I have a template, attaching here: https://redwood.internal/compliance/templates/retention-exception-template (CS/Infra please use and attach to ticket).

Priya Kapoor: there's a second mitigation I pushed: switched the pool to sample-level logging and disabled request bodies for KestrelBank to limit further PII exposure while we stabilize. Command: `rwctl cluster set-logging --pool aurora-dedicated-03 --level sample --drop-request-body true`

Ethan Park: confirmed. Error rate dropped ~35% after scaling and routing changes. No further unredacted logs being written from this point.

Jasmine Patel: I'm coming on for the next shift in 20m. Priya — please hand off any open action items.

Priya Kapoor: handoff to Jasmine: items to track — (1) Compliance ticket link (pending), (2) Confirm deletion after 14 days and post deletion proof, (3) follow-up with KestrelBank DPO. Access list: Priya Kapoor (SRE), Ethan Park (Infra). Incident still in monitoring.

Jasmine Patel: ack, taking over. I'll set a calendar reminder for deletion + follow up with Maya on the compliance ticket.

Maya Chen: I'll watch the compliance ticket and will sign off once the retention override form is filed and KestrelBank DPO confirms. Also — if we need to preserve additional logs for legal hold, do not delete until Legal explicitly instructs.

Priya Kapoor: noted. Closing immediate mitigation work and leaving monitoring. Will update INC-1836004321 timeline with actions performed. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-1836004321 status updated to MONITORING. Next notification scheduled in 30m.
